title: Bhojpuri wedding songs have a home in Mauritius
body: In Mauritius, the Bhojpuri Geet-Gawai tradition brings people together for songs and music before weddings. UNESCO added the practice to its intangible heritage list in 2016.
takeaway: A language can travel with migrants and keep a place in ceremonies generations later.
visual: a group of women singing together around a small drum before a Mauritian wedding

title: Georgian winemakers ferment grapes in buried clay vessels
body: The qvevri is a large egg-shaped clay vessel used in Georgian winemaking. Makers place the grape juice and solids inside, seal the opening and leave the buried vessel to hold the wine as it ferments and matures.
takeaway: In this method, one vessel takes the place of separate containers for several stages.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Qvevri Wine-making Method (2013)
visual: the open mouth of a large clay vessel sunk flush into a cellar floor

title: Making traditional tortillas starts by treating maize with lime
body: In Mexico, maize for tortillas is traditionally treated with slaked lime, an alkaline mineral. The process, called nixtamalisation, loosens the hull and makes the grain easier to grind into dough.
takeaway: What looks like one simple staple begins with a chemical change in the grain.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Traditional Mexican Cuisine (2010)
visual: hands shaping maize dough beside a grinding stone
